notes:
40 stations, numbered 121-160 with no gaps. The list has no sub-headings, so every row's coast is the section heading. I trimmed the leading spaces from each fragment and kept everything else exactly as printed.

Asterisks: I counted 23 (121-127, 129, 131, 132, 134, 137, 138, 144, 146, 147, 149, 150, 152, 153, 155, 156, 159). The text says 24 returns. The list doesn't show which return is missing a mark. One possibility is Milford (High), 139. It has no asterisk, but its keeper is G. Baker, the same as the marked Milford (Low), 138. The note '(These two are looked upon as one station)' sits on line 2460, below 139, and I put it in 139's fragments and other. It reads like a brace joining 138 and 139, but no brace mark is printed.

How I filled the fields:
- Duty titles (P. K., mate, gunner) are in other, not in keepers. Where a row names two people (123, 126), I added the person's name in brackets to show who holds which title. That bracketed name is my addition. Where an other value joins two printed pieces, I separated them with '; '.
- Light descriptions (fixed, white, red, revolving) went into character, and heights into other. Two rows mix the two too closely to split, so I put each whole description in character: Bideford (150) and Nash High (144).
- For 128 'North Stack, Fog Horn Station.' and 151 'Lundy Fog Gun Station.' I put the station kind ('Fog Horn Station', 'Fog Gun Station') in type. These are fog-signal stations, not L.H. or L.V. Lundy appears twice, as 151 (fog gun) and 152 (L.H.), with different keepers.
- Where a row wraps, I joined the wrapped parts of the name, character or other with a space: 147 'Amos' + 'Russell', 150 'Edwd.' + 'Roberts', and the long Nash and Milford text.

Spellings and other things to watch, all kept as printed:
- 'Air' (124) is presumably Point of Ayr.
- 'Caldy' (140) is Caldey.
- 'Sevenstones' (157) is Seven Stones.
- 'Wolfrock' (158) is the Wolf Rock.
- 'Prichard' (127) is as printed.
- 'Syren' (138) is as printed.
- 143 prints the keeper only as a surname, after a dash: 'L.H.--Wilson.'
- W. Bowen is the keeper at both Caernarvon Bay L.V. (130) and Trevose Head (154). This may be two different men; check before treating them as one person.
- Bull Point (134) is in North Devon, but it is printed between Cardigan Bay and South Bishop in Wales, out of geographical order. Its number may not reflect where it is.
- Nash High (144) mentions 'Tuskar Buoy'. This is in the source; I haven't checked it.
- Breaksea (145), Cardigan Bay (133) and Bishop Rock (160) have no keeper named.
